_README: EXAMPLE Apple App Site Association (AASA) file for Buzz passkeys.
WHAT THIS IS: the signed app's passkey ceremonies (src/passkey_ceremony.rs)
are bound to a relying-party domain; Apple verifies that binding against
this file, served by the RP domain over HTTPS. Nothing here is live — this
is a template for the RELEASE-REPO deployment work (buzz-releases signs
the app; the RP domain serves this file).
SERVED BY THE RELAY (single source of truth): the relay serves exactly the
document below — everything except this _README key — at
GET /.well-known/apple-app-site-association
when BUZZ_PASSKEY_TEAM_ID is configured (BUZZ_PASSKEY_BUNDLE_ID defaults to
the desktop identifier in tauri.conf.json), with
Content-Type: application/json
Cache-Control: no-cache
The body is built by `aasa_body` in crates/buzz-relay/src/router.rs; the
test `aasa_example_matches_the_served_aasa` pins this file to that builder,
and `scripts/passkey-activation-check.sh` (activation step 0) fetches the
live URL and checks it against this shape. Use this file only to host the
AASA on a domain NOT served by the relay (CDN / static host).
WHERE TO SERVE IT:
https://<RP-DOMAIN>/.well-known/apple-app-site-association
- Content-Type: application/json (no file extension; do NOT redirect)
- served over HTTPS with a valid certificate
- both with and without the 'www' host prefix should reach the same
content if either host is used as the RP id
WHAT TO REPLACE:
<TEAMID>   - the Apple Developer Team ID that signs the Buzz app
(BUZZ_PASSKEY_TEAM_ID on the relay)
<BUNDLEID> - the Buzz app bundle identifier (CFBundleIdentifier),
app identifier xyz.block.buzz.app (matches tauri.conf.json)
The resulting entry is '<TEAMID>.<BUNDLEID>'.
MUST MATCH (all three, exactly):
1. this file's webcredentials.apps entry, on the RP domain
2. the com.apple.developer.associated-domains entitlement in
Entitlements.plist: 'webcredentials:<RP-DOMAIN>'
3. BUZZ_PASSKEY_RP_ID=<RP-DOMAIN> in the app's runtime environment
If they diverge, passkey ceremonies fail loudly (ASAuthorizationError)
or bind the credential to the wrong RP — the in-contract WebAuthn
validator checks the recorded rpId/origin against exactly these.
VERIFY after deployment (step 0 of the activation runbook):
bash scripts/passkey-activation-check.sh
(Apple caches AASA fetches; allow up to ~24h after a change)
